title: Run L10 before the Llama walkthrough

Continue to L10B for the recorded Llama choices, then run L11 with its default False setting.

title: Run L10B: watch Llama choose a tool
points: Run the whole L10B cell. Change SCENARIO to inspect each saved episode.
note: Run L10 first. In the new L10B cell the helper validates the original JSON reply against the parsed journal and trace, then displays the recorded episode. Change only SCENARIO to inspect the other two episodes. The following slides show selected fields from the same replay. This cell makes no model request and performs no new electrical solve. At the end, run L11 at its default False setting before L12. Llama reasons are historical public returned text. Their correctness must be judged against the input and tool results. SCENARIO can be voltage, restoration or cyber. The full cell is shown.

title: Voltage: Llama asks to check the saved controller
points: Llama identifies the missing check. The current failure forces a new trial.
note: Read the exact reason. The model was offered VERIFY_SAC_FIRST or REVIEW. The application then checks the saved SAC action in OpenDSS. 111.966607% refers to the allowed current, which was 80% of nominal, so this exceeds the configured allowance. The numerical result records two current violations. This P3 full supplied MV/LV study is separate from L2 and L3 test_01. Ask the audience to predict the next allowed step before advancing.

title: Voltage: Llama chooses the existing fallback plan

note: The model selects USE_MPC_PLAN from two allowed choices, the other being REVIEW. It does not invent or solve MPC. The recorded context already supplies a plan and its eligibility. The application performs a fresh numerical check at that historical time. The result is just below the allowed current threshold. No operating permission follows from this check alone. Ask which evidence, rather than wording, makes the fallback eligible for review.

title: Restoration: Llama chooses a useful new trial
points: The new trial serves more load, keeps critical service and passes the current check.
note: Switch L10B to restoration. This is the separate L10 feeder-catalog restoration study, not the L6 six-node MILP. The recorded protocol requires a first refinement but Llama chooses between the offered fractions. SHED_075 disconnects 75% of the ordered noncritical load objects, not 75% of load kW. The exact reason calls improvement a possibility. Python evaluates the trial and finds improved service while the tie loading remains 91.867215% of its allowance. A useful hypothesis becomes evidence only after that check.

title: Restoration: the next trial crosses the current limit
points: The next trial fails the current limit. Keep the previous passed candidate.
note: Keep the actual returned reason visible. It refers to a target in the objective, but its claim should not be accepted as a proved fact. In this record the next trial is numerically rejected for a thermal failure. Restoring more load does not make a failed current check acceptable. Ask participants to explain why the previous passed candidate must remain in the case record. The model’s trial budget is bounded.

title: Restoration: catch Llama’s wrong ranking
points: The returned order is wrong. Python chooses the smaller cost and rechecks the plan.
note: Let pairs answer before discussing the result. Smaller cost is better, so E03 must rank before E02. Llama returns [E02,E03] while its explanation claims lowest score first. The recorded language_order_agrees_with_cost field is False. A deterministic guard retains E03 and rechecks it as E05, with no recorded failures. Human acknowledgment and dispatch remain False. The paired fixed workflow reaches the same final action and cost. This example motivates verification rather than an unsupported superiority claim.

title: Finish L12: practice the readback
points: Run all of L12 after completing L0–L11 in notebook order.
Check wrong-ID rejection, simulated acknowledgment and equipment_dispatch=False.
source_label: Classroom_Labs.ipynb, L12; cell classroom-033; simulated readback only.
note: This cell returns to the original test_01 voltage result through selected_trials. It does not use the restoration or cyber sweeps. Read both scope outcomes and explain why the full MV/LV request remains HOLD. The new simulated acknowledgment grants no physical operating authority and does not complete the review of an old record. Readback means repeating the recommendation ID and conditions so the acknowledgment can be matched to the same proposal. In this exercise it is simulated. Check the wrong-ID rejection, the correct simulated acknowledgment and equipment_dispatch=False.

title: Start a control-room pilot with a clear study request
points: Use an approved copy of the network data with a time stamp, topology version and limits.
If required data are missing or too old, return HOLD and name the missing information.
note: Proposed advisory pilot, not a deployment claim. F12 is an illustrative teaching feeder name. Read the study request aloud: compare the allowed voltage-support options, keep the stated current and voltage limits, show the worst margins and missing checks, and return a recommendation for review. The data owner defines acceptable age, source and quality rules. L1 and L7 illustrate matching inputs to results, but hashes alone do not authenticate those sources.
caption: Proposed advisory pilot — teaching design. F12 is an illustrative identifier.
source_label: Teaching proposal informed by NIST OT guidance and the cited notebook checks.

title: Give the assistant a small, controlled tool list
points: An approved interface supplies read-only data and study tools. Log every request and result.
Keep equipment commands in the utility’s separate authorized operating process.
note: Proposed advisory pilot. Walk through the lanes: operator, assistant, application-controlled tool gateway and engineering tools. Llama requests one permitted function; the application checks the request and executes the tool. A snapshot identifier binds the result to the input. The workshop Python functions are teaching counterparts, not SCADA adapters. NIST OT guidance supports controlled information flows, least privilege and logging. The exact pilot architecture is our teaching recommendation, not a NIST-certified design.
caption: Proposed advisory pilot — teaching design. Classroom functions are not live control-room interfaces.
source_label: Teaching proposal informed by NIST OT guidance and the cited notebook checks.

title: Check three things before returning a proposal
points: Check that the inputs match, the required limits pass and the required network parts were modeled.
Example: an MV-only PASS stays on HOLD when the request requires the full MV/LV network.
note: Proposed advisory pilot. Current data and a matching evidence packet are the first gate. The second gate checks stated engineering limits with approved tools. The third asks whether the calculations cover the request, including excluded low-voltage parts or required protection and dynamic studies. This is not a universal complete security checklist. It illustrates why L12 can produce a passing local calculation and still HOLD a broader request. Make missing evidence visible instead of allowing fluent text to fill the gap.
caption: Proposed advisory pilot — teaching design. A PASS is limited to its tested model and inputs.
source_label: Teaching proposal informed by NIST OT guidance and the cited notebook checks.

title: Give the operator a short evidence packet
points: Show the input snapshot, selected option, worst margins, rejected trials and missing checks.
The reviewer can ask for another study, reject the proposal or accept it for the next review step.
note: Proposed advisory pilot. Use three review questions: Does this match the current equipment, inputs and model? Did the required checks pass, with missing checks clear? What exactly am I approving, who owns the next step, and where is the record? Record the reviewer, reason, case snapshot and tool versions. Accepting a study result does not itself issue an equipment command. Authorized operating procedures and roles determine any later physical action. L12 practices only a simulated ID-bound readback.
caption: Proposed advisory pilot — teaching design. Review of a study is distinct from operating equipment.
source_label: Teaching proposal informed by NIST OT guidance and the cited notebook checks.

title: Adopt it in stages and measure the benefit
points: Begin with past cases, then read-only shadow work, then a limited pilot with named reviewers.
Compare against the same tools in a fixed script: correct studies, missed checks, time and rework.
note: Proposed advisory pilot. Historical replay lets engineers define expected outcomes and failure cases. Shadow use compares recommendations alongside the existing process without relying on them for equipment control. A limited pilot needs a named owner, training, an agreed scope and a way to stop use. Measure end-to-end elapsed time including review, correct completed studies, missed or stale inputs, overlooked limits and reviewer changes. Compare the same engineering tools with and without Llama. Our paired records show identical final numerical results, so there is no basis yet to promise higher accuracy, less operator workload or faster decisions. NIST AI RMF supports human roles, evaluation under realistic conditions and deactivation; these particular pilot metrics are our recommendation.
caption: Proposed advisory pilot — teaching design. Benefits must be measured against an appropriate baseline.
source_label: Teaching proposal informed by NIST OT guidance and the cited notebook checks.

title: Save a workshop record others can repeat
points: Save your changed inputs and results, labeled new, archived or simulated.
Explain the request, tool call, result, checks and next decision.
note: Use the final three minutes for pair reports and saving. Each pair names one changed parameter, compares its predicted and observed result, and states one evidence limit. Another person should be able to repeat the experiment from the saved notebook. The reading guide supplies the full source links, stable cell map and debrief answers.
